title: The HSSC Constable Recruitment Paper Leak Scam
dek: A Jammu-based printing agency contracted to prepare Haryana's police constable exam papers instead became the source of a leak sold on to candidates for up to Rs 10 lakh each — an investigation that produced 167 arrests over the following years.

promise.quote: Recruitment to Haryana Police constable posts will be conducted through the Haryana Staff Selection Commission on the basis of a securely printed and distributed question paper.

promise.context: This reflects HSSC's standard institutional mandate for the male constable recruitment exam, rather than a verified quotation from a specific HSSC statement, which this entry has not located.

target.description: A written exam for male police constable posts conducted on the basis of a question paper kept confidential from the printing stage through to the exam itself.

reality.description: HSSC had contracted a Jammu-based examination agency to set and print question papers for the male constable recruitment exam, scheduled for 7 and 8 August 2021 (morning and evening shifts each day). According to the investigation, a manager at the agency's printing press, Rakesh Kumar, had a soft copy of the exam on a pen drive by 31 July 2021; another employee, Jitender Singh, copied the questions and answer key from that pen drive around 2 August and prepared hard copies. The paper and answer key were then allegedly sold on — one accused, Raj Kumar, reportedly sold them to associates for Rs 1 crore, who in turn sold the answer key to individual aspirants for around Rs 10 lakh each. The leak came to light on 7 August 2021 when a Kaithal police CIA team apprehended three individuals with material linked to the leak; HSSC subsequently cancelled the exam. Haryana Police's SIT continued making arrests for years afterward, with the total reaching 167 by 2025.
